questions.prompt: Would you change your habits? How will you get to work this year?

answers.label: Cycle
answers.explanation: No fuel at all, and it keeps you fit. The lowest-carbon way to get to work.

answers.label: Drive
answers.explanation: Driving alone burns the most fuel per person of any option here.

answers.label: Carpool
answers.explanation: Sharing a car halves each person's emissions, but it still burns petrol every day.

answers.label: Take a taxi each day
answers.explanation: A taxi burns as much fuel as driving yourself, plus the empty trips between fares.

questions.prompt: Your power plan is up for renewal. What do you pick?

answers.label: Keep things as they are
answers.explanation: Nothing changes, so neither does the carbon footprint.

answers.label: A 100% renewable plan
answers.explanation: Power from wind, sun and water instead of burning gas or coal.

answers.label: Add a gas patio heater
answers.explanation: Heating outdoor air with gas burns fuel for very little warmth.

answers.label: Install a gas-heated spa pool
answers.explanation: Keeping a spa pool hot with gas burns fuel all year round.

questions.prompt: Planning the week's meals. What's on the menu?

answers.label: Red meat most nights
answers.explanation: Beef and lamb produce a lot of methane and need far more land and feed than other foods.

answers.label: A bit of everything
answers.explanation: A balanced plate, but the meat still adds to the footprint.

answers.label: Mostly imported, air-freighted treats
answers.explanation: Food flown in from overseas burns a lot of fuel to reach your plate.

answers.label: Mostly local vegetables
answers.explanation: Vegetables take far less land, water and energy to grow than meat, and local food travels less.

questions.prompt: Time for a summer break. Where are you heading?

answers.label: Explore the local bush tracks
answers.explanation: Exploring close to home uses little fuel and keeps money in the local area.

answers.label: A train trip to the next town
answers.explanation: Trains are an efficient way to travel, though the trip still uses some energy.

answers.label: A long road trip around the country
answers.explanation: Long drives burn plenty of petrol.

answers.label: A long-haul flight overseas
answers.explanation: Flying long distances burns a huge amount of fuel; one trip can outweigh a year of driving.

questions.prompt: The council offers a free compost bin. Do you take it?

answers.label: Take it, but rarely use it
answers.explanation: A bin that sits unused doesn't keep scraps out of landfill.

answers.label: No thanks, it all goes in the bin
answers.explanation: Food waste in landfill breaks down without air and releases methane, a strong greenhouse gas.

answers.label: Yes, and start composting
answers.explanation: Food scraps in landfill rot into methane. Composting turns them into soil instead.

answers.label: No thanks, I burn my garden waste
answers.explanation: Burning green waste releases its carbon straight into the air, along with smoke.

questions.prompt: Your old car needs replacing. What do you buy?

answers.label: A big petrol ute
answers.explanation: Big petrol vehicles burn the most fuel every kilometre.

answers.label: An e-bike instead
answers.explanation: An e-bike uses a tiny amount of electricity and replaces many short car trips.

answers.label: A large petrol SUV
answers.explanation: A heavy petrol SUV burns far more fuel than a small car.

answers.label: A hybrid
answers.explanation: A hybrid uses less petrol than a regular car, but still burns it.

questions.prompt: Winter is coming. How will you keep the house warm?

answers.label: Just a heat pump
answers.explanation: Heat pumps are very efficient, but an uninsulated house lets much of the heat escape.

answers.label: Insulate and use a heat pump
answers.explanation: Insulation keeps the heat in, so an efficient heat pump has far less work to do.

answers.label: Gas heater on all day
answers.explanation: Burning gas all day releases carbon dioxide the whole time it's on.

answers.label: An open coal fire
answers.explanation: Coal is one of the most carbon-heavy fuels, and open fires send much of the heat up the chimney.

questions.prompt: Your phone still works, but a new model is out. What do you do?

answers.label: Upgrade to the newest model
answers.explanation: Making a new phone uses lots of energy and materials, even when the old one still works.

answers.label: Buy a refurbished one
answers.explanation: Reusing a phone avoids most of the cost of making a new one, but still adds a little.

answers.label: Keep using it
answers.explanation: Most of a phone's footprint comes from making it, so using it longer is the cleanest option.

answers.label: Buy the new one and keep the old as a spare
answers.explanation: A second phone means making a new one while the old one sits in a drawer.

questions.prompt: Neighbours are organising a weekend tree-planting day. Do you join?

answers.label: Join and bring friends
answers.explanation: More hands means more trees, and trees take in carbon as they grow.

answers.label: Skip it this time
answers.explanation: No harm done, but no trees planted either.

answers.label: Skip it and go for a long drive
answers.explanation: A long drive for fun burns fuel, and no trees get planted.

answers.label: Clear the bush on your section instead
answers.explanation: Clearing plants releases the carbon they store and leaves the soil bare.

questions.prompt: Your work offers a work-from-home day each week. Do you take it?

answers.label: No, I'll keep driving in
answers.explanation: Driving in every day keeps the commute's emissions going all year.

answers.label: Now and then
answers.explanation: Occasional days at home help a little, but most trips still happen.

answers.label: Yes, but drive out for lunch
answers.explanation: Driving out for lunch adds a car trip, so the day at home saves little.

answers.label: Yes, and walk to the local café
answers.explanation: Skipping the commute one day a week saves that trip's fuel, and walking adds none.
